source: Ye et al. (2023) SATLM: Satisfiability-Aided Language Models
finding: An LLM writes declarative constraints (not a step-by-step program) and a SAT/SMT solver (Z3) does the search. This beat chain-of-thought and program-aided prompting on most tasks.
numbers: code-davinci-002, greedy: GSM-SYS 69.4 (CoT 46.5, ProgLM 43.4); ALGEBRA 77.5 (CoT 53.6); LSAT 35.0 (CoT 23.5); BoardgameQA 79.4 (CoT 60.7); CLUTRR 68.3 (ProgLM 58.9); ProofWriter 99.7 (ProgLM 83.7).
limits: Old models (2023). On plain GSM, SATLM 71.8 vs ProgLM 72.7 greedy, so no gain on easy arithmetic. Hand-written few-shot prompts.
agent_relevance: Offloading search to a solver works when the model only has to translate. S4 TEST could use a solver call for constraint checks.

source: Ye et al. (2023) SATLM: Satisfiability-Aided Language Models
finding: With self-consistency, SATLM set new SoTA on LSAT and BoardgameQA, beating models trained on the full training set.
numbers: LSAT 30.9 -> 37.4; BoardgameQA 73.9 -> 80.7; GSM 84.8 with self-consistency (+2.4 over ProgLM); GSM-SYS 80.9 with self-consistency in the text. Bootstrap tests significant.
limits: Only 5 samples used on long-prompt tasks (LSAT, BoardgameQA, ProofWriter), 40 on the rest. One table row lists 53.4 for a self-consistency cell that conflicts with the 80.9 in the text; parse of table is unclear.
agent_relevance: Combine solver checks with sampling; gains can stack.

source: Ye et al. (2023) SATLM: Satisfiability-Aided Language Models
finding: The solver gives a free error signal: UNSAT and AMBIGUOUS verdicts let the system abstain. Selective accuracy is higher than for program-aided LMs.
numbers: Selective accuracy on GSM-SYS 77% (SATLM) vs 45% (ProgLM). SATLM answers fewer questions but gets more correct on GSM-SYS and CLUTRR.
limits: Coverage is lower; a fallback answer is still needed when the solver fails.
agent_relevance: A solver verdict (SAT / UNSAT / ambiguous) is a cheap trigger for S4 TEST to reject a formalisation or ask for a rewrite.

source: Ye et al. (2023) SATLM: Satisfiability-Aided Language Models
finding: The gain generalises across LLMs but shrinks for weak ones.
numbers: Table 6 greedy: gpt-3.5-turbo GSM-SYS 63.4 vs ProgLM 51.2, CLUTRR 50.6 vs 45.9, ProofWriter 96.4; text-davinci-003 GSM-SYS 63.6 vs 40.4. Weak code-davinci-001: GSM-SYS 16.5 vs 15.5, GSM 34.2 vs 35.6, LSAT 19.6.
limits: A weak model cannot write correct constraints, so the solver adds little. Gain depends on parse quality.
agent_relevance: Translation quality is the bottleneck, not solving. Verify the formalisation step.

source: Pan et al. (2023) Logic-LM: Empowering LLMs with Symbolic Solvers for Faithful Logical Reasoning
finding: LLM translates the problem; a solver runs it (Z3 for AR-LSAT analytical problems, Prover9 for FOL, Pyke for deduction, python-constraint for CSP). A self-refiner uses solver error messages to repair the formalisation.
numbers: Average gain 39.2% over standard prompting and 18.4% over CoT (GPT-3.5). GPT-4, Logic-LM vs CoT: PrOntoQA 83.20 vs 98.79 (worse); ProofWriter 79.66 vs 68.11; FOLIO 78.92 vs 70.58; LogicalDeduction 87.63 vs 75.25; AR-LSAT 43.04 vs 35.06.
limits: On PrOntoQA GPT-4 CoT beats Logic-LM. 600 examples sampled per dataset for cost. Gain over standard prompting is largest on non-linear tasks (FOLIO +21.85, LogicalDeduction +45.67, AR-LSAT +24.14).
agent_relevance: Solver tools help most when the problem needs hypothesis, case split and elimination, which is what DPLL does and forward-chaining CoT does badly.

source: Pan et al. (2023) Logic-LM: Empowering LLMs with Symbolic Solvers for Faithful Logical Reasoning
finding: Self-refinement from solver errors raises the share of executable formalisations, but accuracy plateaus after the first rounds.
numbers: Exe_Rate GPT-4: AR-LSAT 32.6% -> 39.8%, FOLIO 79.9% -> 85.8%; GPT-3.5: FOLIO 66.7% -> 84.3%, AR-LSAT 11.3% -> 21.8%. GPT-4 AR-LSAT Exe_Acc stays 58.8-60.0. Rounds 0-3 tested on FOLIO.
limits: Only grammar errors reach the refiner; semantic errors do not. Even after refinement only 39.8% of GPT-4 AR-LSAT formalisations execute.
agent_relevance: Solver error text is a useful repair signal, but a syntax-valid wrong formula passes silently. Add a semantic check.

source: Pan et al. (2023) Logic-LM: Empowering LLMs with Symbolic Solvers for Faithful Logical Reasoning
finding: Solver-based reasoning degrades more slowly with proof depth than CoT.
numbers: 300 ProofWriter examples per depth subset (0, <=1, <=2, <=3, <=5 hops). Logic-LM advantage over CoT grows with depth (Figure 3).
limits: Per-depth values are in a figure only.
agent_relevance: Longer chains favour tools over pure text reasoning.

source: Wei et al. (2025) SATBench: Benchmarking LLMs' Logical Reasoning via Automated Puzzle Generation from SAT Formulas
finding: 2,100 story puzzles generated from CNF formulas. Accuracy falls as clauses rise and reasoning is weak on hard UNSAT.
numbers: o4-mini overall 89.3 (hard SAT 91.1, hard UNSAT 65.0); DeepSeek-R1 87.8; DeepSeek-V3 84.0; DeepSeek-Distill-7B 43.9. Average hard accuracy over all models 53.0 vs 50 random. Easy = 4-19 clauses, hard = 31-50.
quote: A stated UNSAT from a model on a large constraint set is not trustworthy without a solver.
limits: Binary label, so 50% is chance. Human passing rate above 90% on a sample of 100.
agent_relevance: High accuracy on easy puzzles hides collapse: GPT-4o is near 50% at 30 clauses.

source: Wei et al. (2025) SATBench: Benchmarking LLMs' Logical Reasoning via Automated Puzzle Generation from SAT Formulas
finding: Models say SAT without a valid assignment (satisfiability bias). A right label does not mean right reasoning.
numbers: Trace accuracy: o4-mini SAT label 94.7 but trace 74.6; DS-R1 85.2 vs 73.8; Claude-3.7 SAT label 83.2, trace 47.4. Errors in o4-mini: satisfiability bias 68.7%, condition omission 14.3%; DS-R1: 40.5%, 12.6%.
limits: Traces judged by GPT-4o; error types classified by GPT-4o. Other types: context inconsistency, spurious priors.
agent_relevance: Check the witness (assignment) against every clause; the label alone is not evidence.

source: Wei et al. (2025) SATBench: Benchmarking LLMs' Logical Reasoning via Automated Puzzle Generation from SAT Formulas
finding: Narrative wrapping costs little for the strongest models; formula-only input is slightly easier.
numbers: Puzzle vs raw CNF accuracy: DeepSeek-V3 84.0 vs 87.3; o4-mini 89.4 vs 94.3.
limits: Small gap, so most of the difficulty is the search itself.
agent_relevance: Failure is in search, not in reading the text.

source: Pan et al. (2025) Can Transformers Reason Logically? A Study in SAT Solving
finding: Proof by construction that a decoder-only Transformer with chain-of-thought can decide 3-SAT using backtracking and unit deduction, with O(p^2) parameters (7 layers, 5 heads).
numbers: Compiled model perfect on all eval sets. CoT length stayed within 8p to 20.08p, far under the worst-case p*2^(p+1), so deduction prunes the search.
limits: Non-uniform: one network per max size (p variables, c clauses). Worst case is still exponential CoT.
agent_relevance: Formal support that an explicit stepwise trace with backtracking is the right shape for SAT-like checking.

source: Pan et al. (2025) Can Transformers Reason Logically? A Study in SAT Solving
finding: A Transformer trained on DPLL-style reasoning paths learns it in-distribution but does not extend to bigger formulas.
numbers: Trained on p in [6,10] or [11,15]: SAT/UNSAT accuracy 99.8-100% across train/test distributions; full-trace accuracy 86.06-99.40% (lowest 86.06, skewed test, marginal-trained, p 11-15). 10,000 samples per cell. Limited length generalisation beyond training p.
limits: Small scale; trained from scratch, not a pretrained LLM. Cites Zhang et al. 2023: single-pass Transformers without CoT fail to generalise across distributions.
agent_relevance: Trace training needs matching size; do not expect learned search to scale by itself.

source: Selsam et al. (2019) Learning a SAT Solver from Single-Bit Supervision (NeuroSAT)
finding: A message-passing network trained only on the satisfiable/unsatisfiable bit learns to find satisfying assignments, and improves when run for more iterations at test time.
numbers: SR(40) test accuracy 85%; decodes a satisfying assignment for over 70% of satisfiable problems; with extra iterations solves 25% of SR(200) satisfiable problems (under 10% at the training iteration count).
limits: Early neural SAT: far behind CDCL; small sizes; trained on a random SR(n) distribution only.
agent_relevance: More inference rounds can improve accuracy: an early sign of test-time compute scaling.

source: Hazra et al. (2024) Can LLMs Reason? A Characterization via 3-SAT
finding: GPT-4 shows an easy-hard-easy curve over the clause/variable ratio, with accuracy near 10% in the hard region (SAT Search). Letting the LLM translate to MiniSat input gives about 100%.
numbers: Critical ratio alpha_c about 4.267. GPT-4 Turbo SAT Search about 10% in the hard region; SAT-Translate with an external solver about 100% across all alpha. GPT-4 does better when many assignments satisfy the formula.
limits: Small formulas (n up to 10 variables); menu-selection puzzle format; only GPT-4 shows a solver-like phase transition among the models tested.
agent_relevance: Matches our design: the model translates and the tool searches.

source: Hazra et al. (2025) Have LLMs Learned to Reason? A Characterization via 3-SAT Phase Transition
finding: All non-reasoning LLMs drop to near 10% in the hard 3-SAT region. DeepSeek R1 is the exception: its hard-region accuracy exceeds other models' easy-region accuracy.
numbers: Models: GPT-4o, Gemini 2.0 Flash, Claude 3.7 Sonnet, DeepSeek V3, R1. About 5000 formulas, n in [1,10]. Checked with MiniSat 2.2, model counts by D4. R1 near-perfect on 2-SAT and Horn-SAT; others dip near the 2-SAT threshold c=1. In-context examples did not help in the hard region.
limits: Exact R1 percentages are only in plots. Formulas are tiny. R1 detects satisfiable formulas well but often fails to produce the assignment (limited completeness).
agent_relevance: R1 output tokens grow polynomially with input size; traces look like in-context tree search. Suggests budgeted search tokens, not prompts, help.

source: Hazra et al. (2025) Have LLMs Learned to Reason? A Characterization via 3-SAT Phase Transition
finding: R1 accuracy is flat in the satisfiability ratio, unlike other LLMs, which do better when many assignments satisfy the formula (a shortcut). This looks like a real search procedure.
numbers: Other LLMs: accuracy rises with model_count / 2^n. R1: consistent regardless, like a classical solver. Distilled Qwen series: reasoning improves with size.
limits: Qualitative trace study; failure cases exist where R1 and GPT-4o call a satisfiable formula unsatisfiable.
agent_relevance: Test the agent on instances with few solutions, where shortcuts fail.

source: Zhang, Chen, Chen (2026) Satisfiability Solving with LLMs: A Matched-Pair Evaluation of Reasoning Capability
finding: Standard metrics mislead: models label nearly all formulas satisfiable, do not show the easy-hard-easy signature, and fail as variable count grows. Paired SAT/UNSAT formulas with the Accurate Differentiation Rate (ADR) expose true skill.
numbers: 70 SAT/UNSAT pairs per variable count. GPT-5 ADR 0.79 at 25 variables, 0.35 at 50 (only about 20% of runs completed at 50). Past 25 variables all models except GPT-5 sit near 0.5 accuracy and ADR often below 0.2. Example: accuracy 0.77 but ADR 0.60.
limits: Budget limited o1 and deepseek-reasoner to 75 variables and others to 60. Mostly 2-SAT and 3-SAT plus Vertex Cover and 3D-packing reductions.
agent_relevance: Test items in pairs that differ by one clause and flip the label; grade both.

source: Zhang, Chen, Chen (2026) Satisfiability Solving with LLMs: A Matched-Pair Evaluation of Reasoning Capability
finding: Decisions agree across CNF, Vertex Cover and 3D-packing encodings for most models, so the skill transfers across representations.
numbers: Agreement CNF vs Vertex Cover 75.3% of all instances (above 80% for most models); CNF vs 3D packing 80.2%. When different: correct on SAT 73% vs VC 27%; SAT 53% vs packing 47%.
limits: Reduction encoding done by the authors' pipeline; scale degradation persists.
agent_relevance: Re-encoding a problem is a cheap consistency test for S4.

source: Lin et al. (2025) ZebraLogic: On the Scaling Limits of LLMs for Logical Reasoning
finding: Logic grid puzzles as CSPs; accuracy collapses as search space and Z3 conflicts (a DPLL/CDCL-style measure) grow. The authors call it the curse of complexity.
numbers: Overall: o1-full 81.0, o1-preview 71.4, o1-mini 59.7, Sonnet-3.5 36.2, Llama-3.1-405B 32.6 (medium 22.5, large 1.5, X-large 0.0), GPT-4o 31.7. Best-of-N oracle on GPT-4o: 60.3 (N=32), 69.1 (N=128); majority vote 38.0 (N=32), 37.6 (N=128).
limits: Table columns read from pdftotext layout; row alignment for DeepSeek-R1 uncertain, so R1 not quoted.
agent_relevance: Solver conflict count predicts model difficulty; sampling more helps only with an oracle verifier.

source: Sun et al. (2024) AutoSAT: Automatically Optimize SAT Solvers via LLMs
finding: GPT-4o rewrites heuristic functions inside a small CDCL solver (EasySAT, 5k tokens) guided by a hill climber or a (1+1) evolutionary algorithm; fitness is PAR2 on a dataset.
numbers: Beats MiniSat on 9 of 12 datasets and Kissat on 4. PAR2 gain over EasySAT from 7.86% (KnightTour) to 88.22% (register-allocation). Example: social-golfer EasySAT 10,000 (0 solved) -> 1,178 (18 solved, EA). Kissat still far better on SCP (76 vs 9,077) and KnightTour (146 vs 1,649).
limits: Tuned per dataset, so overfitting risk. GHC vs EA winner varies by dataset. Kissat (250k tokens) does not fit in context.
agent_relevance: An evolve-and-measure loop where the measured score is the only judge. Small modules fit the context.

source: Sun et al. (2026) Discovering heuristics in a complex SAT solver with LLMs (AutoModSAT)
finding: Modular MiniSat-based solver (ModSAT), three LLM agents (coder, evaluator, repairer), prompt diversification, presearch pruning and (1+lambda) evolution.
numbers: 40% PAR-2 improvement over baseline ModSAT; over 30% over Kissat and CaDiCaL; 11 datasets (7 from SAT Competition 2023, others from 2024); beats parameter-tuned (SMAC3) variants with equal or more solved instances on 8 of 11. Kissat-para wins on Zamkeller (eliminate=0, simplify=0 explain most of it).
limits: Baseline ModSAT is weaker than Kissat; families with fewer than 20 instances removed to limit overfitting. Without presearch and prompt optimization the generated code was less diverse.
agent_relevance: Prune candidates cheaply before expensive tests.

source: Chen and Li (2025) DaSAThco: Data-Aware SAT Heuristics Combinations Optimization via LLMs
finding: LLM builds a portfolio of heuristic ensembles guided by problem archetypes; a learned selector maps instance features to an ensemble. Targets out-of-domain generalisation, which AutoSAT lacks.
numbers: 1000 s timeout, PAR-2 metric. Best PAR-2 and most solved instances on the tested families; notable gain on PRP (more solved than AutoSAT's 15). On in-domain CoinsGrid a single well-tuned solver still wins.
limits: Table values only partly extracted; the in-domain case shows a portfolio is not always best.
agent_relevance: Instance-aware routing of strategies; analogous to routing problems to operators.

source: Schidler and Szeider (2025) Extracting Problem Structure with LLMs for Optimized SAT Local Search
finding: LLMs read the Python encoding code and generate local-search preprocessing for CaDiCaL in gather and refine phases; works for any instance of the same encoding.
numbers: Used o1-mini, gpt-4o-2024-11-20 and Claude Sonnet; CaDiCaL 1.9.5, PySAT. On Directed Feedback Vertex Set (513 graphs) solved 12 additional instances. o1-mini repairs code in fewer iterations than Sonnet or 4o (limit ten tries).
limits: Models explain parts of the encoding but miss its overall purpose. Gains confined to hard instances.
agent_relevance: Giving a model the generator code, not just instances, lets it exploit structure.

source: Utsho et al. (2026) Empirical Evidence of Complexity-Induced Limits in LLMs on Finite Discrete State-Space Problems
finding: Nine parameterised tasks including Boolean satisfiability, scored with deterministic validators. Reasoning models hold up at low complexity then collapse abruptly past a task-specific threshold.
numbers: Accuracy declines often exceed 50% beyond thresholds; failures include inconsistent traces and incomplete assignments.
limits: Only abstract and intro read for exact numbers; per-task SAT values not extracted.
agent_relevance: Gate the agent: on large constraint sets switch from free reasoning to a tool.

source: Hazra et al. (2024) Can LLMs Reason? A Characterization via 3-SAT
finding: LLM accuracy tracks the solver's own hardness curve: the dip matches the MiniSat runtime spike near alpha_c. LLMs lean on how many solutions exist, not on search.
numbers: Authors argue the dip mimics increased MiniSat solving time in the hard region; accuracy higher for formulas with larger satisfiability ratio (Figure 3 right). GPT-4 Turbo 1106-preview main model; SAT Search is harder than SAT Decision.
limits: Figures only; no numeric table. Small n.
agent_relevance: Hard instances are those with few solutions. Use them to test S4 rather than random ones.
